original_question: Let X be a reflexive Banach space such that every normalized weakly null sequence in X generates, up to equivalence, the same spreading model. Is that unique spreading model necessarily equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 4 ("Unique spreading model problem" – S. A. Argyros)
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the reflexive hypothesis, the fact that the uniqueness is only up to equivalence, the restriction to spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences, and the exact dichotomy asked for in the paper: equivalence to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 <= p < infinity.
missing_details: The paper formulates the hypothesis in the notation |SP_w(X)/~| = 1, where SP_w(X) is the class of all spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X, and ~ is equivalence of basic sequences.

A fully stand-alone formulation should define what it means for a normalized basic sequence (x_n) to generate a sequence (y_n) as a spreading model: there must exist ε_n > 0 with ε_n ↓ 0 such that for every n in N, every scalars a_0,...,a_n in [-1,1], and every n <= k_0 < ... < k_n in N, one has (1+ε_n)^(-1)||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i y_i|| <= ||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i x_{k_i}|| <= (1+ε_n)||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i y_i||.
Strictly speaking, the unique object is a unique equivalence class of basic sequences in SP_w(X), not literally a distinguished sequence until one chooses a representative.
If the question is to be completely self-contained, it should state that the target comparison is with the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p over the same scalar field.

The nearby context in the paper notes that reflexivity is essential and that Problem 4 is stronger than the neighboring Rosenthal basis problem; this helps keep the scope faithful and prevents drifting to the stronger countable-spreading-models variant in Problem 5.
refined_question: Let X be a reflexive Banach space over R or C. For X, let SP_w(X) denote the class of all basic sequences (e_n) that arise as spreading models of normalized weakly null sequences in X in the Brunel-Sucheston sense; namely, there exists a normalized basic sequence (x_n) in X and a sequence ε_n > 0 with ε_n ↓ 0 such that for every n in N, every scalars a_0,...,a_n in [-1,1], and every n <= k_0 < ... < k_n in N, (1+ε_n)^(-1)||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i e_i|| <= ||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i x_{k_i}|| <= (1+ε_n)||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i e_i||. Suppose that SP_w(X) consists of a single equivalence class of basic sequences, i.e. |SP_w(X)/~| = 1, where ~ denotes equivalence of basic sequences. Must that unique spreading model be equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?
justification: The draft matches Section 5, Problem 4 essentially verbatim in mathematical content. The paper first defines generation of a spreading model and the notation SP_w(X), then asks exactly whether a reflexive Banach space with a unique spreading model up to equivalence must have that model equivalent to the canonical basis of c_0 or ℓ_p. The immediately following remarks show that reflexivity is part of the intended statement and that this problem is meant as a stronger neighboring problem than the Rosenthal basis problem, while Problem 5 is a distinct stronger variant with only countably many equivalence classes. So the right refinement is the paper’s Problem 4 itself, made fully stand-alone by unpacking the definition of 'generate as a spreading model' and the notation |SP_w(X)/~| = 1.
